title: Livestock GPS Fence and Straying Alert
dataSources: Beehive telemetry (`beehive:reading`), coop door (`chickencoop:door`), egg counts (`egg:count`), livestock tags (`livestock:tag`), feed level (`feed:level`), pasture sensors (`pasture:sensor`).
app: Homestead sensors — connected beehive scale/temperature/sound, automatic chicken-coop door, egg counter, livestock GPS/health tags, feed-silo level, and pasture soil sensors — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and LoRaWAN gateways.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=livestock:tag
| stats latest(distance_from_center_m) as dist, latest(_time) as seen by animal
| eval strayed=if(dist>pasture_radius_m,1,0), silent=if((now()-seen)>7200,1,0)
| where strayed=1 OR silent=1
description: Alerts when a tagged animal wanders beyond the pasture or a tag goes silent, so a break in the fence is caught quickly.
value: A single strayed animal can mean a downed fence and a lost flock; a location and heartbeat check turns hours of searching into minutes.
implementation: Ingest livestock GPS tags into `index=personal`; alert when an animal leaves the pasture or stops reporting.
visualization: Table of animals outside the fence or gone quiet.
grandmaExplanation: It warns you if an animal wanders out of the field or its tracker goes quiet, so you find a broken fence fast.
